quest.title: Fate's Accursed Wiles
quest.description: The book reveals that Durin is bound by a curse born of prophecy. You recall how a blessing once helped him overcome it in Simulanka — maybe reliving that moment will complete the story...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x475, Mora x49200, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Some say, the god of fate calls the outcome of every dice roll before it's even made.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: And that's why, the secret to winning a lot of games is having that god on your side.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Hehe, your luck is amazing, Kaeya!

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Your turn. Give it another shot.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Fear not, o crimson dragonborn — for I, the Prinzessin der Verurteilung, have bestowed upon you the benediction of the midnight hour, and with it you shall surely smite this usurper.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Mein Fräulein means to say, she's rooting for you in secret. Oh, and that you must — at all costs — defeat the one who snatched her limited-edition card back.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hm...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: I'm... not too sure if that counts as good luck, or bad?

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Ahaha... 'Tis naught but the perfidious machinations of fate!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Miss} Honorary Knight and Paimon! You're back!

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: It's good to see you, Honorary Knight. Mein Fräulein is quite invested in the outcome of this match, so please, allow me to extend greetings on her behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! Um, but if you're all playing cards, how come you're not over at The Cat's Tail?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: There's something about our horned friend over there that seems to frighten off little animals. Could be because he used to be a dragon...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Normally, the animals just steer clear of him, but in the close confines of The Cat's Tail...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Let's just say, the feline residents probably consider it "their turf" — and we all know how dangerous a cornered cat can be...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, Durin got scratched?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I just wanted to borrow one of their nests for a nap...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: One of their nests? Wait, you mean... a cat sofa!?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Yeah. It's more comfortable for me... I can stretch out just the way I like. But, it turns out, the black cat and his minions are quite territorial...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Luckily, Miss Diona helped smooth things over, and they finally agreed to let me use one.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: But, uh... I only get to use it after dark.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tough luck, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Diona stepped in! Y'know, underneath it all, she really does like helping people.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: The more likely reason is because Durin won't touch a drop of alcohol. As far as Diona's concerned, that pretty much makes them two peas in a pod. It's a shame, really, considering everything Mondstadt has to offer in that regard...

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Hmph!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Mondstadt's alcoholic drinks are a bit too much for me to handle right now. But maybe someday...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's no need to force it. Who says you have to drink just 'cause you're in Mondstadt?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's just... I'd really like to make some more friends, so I need to learn how humans socialize. I guess alcohol is usually involved, though...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: But, that's why I started learning how to play Genius Invokation TCG. It's also a kind of social activity, but it doesn't involve drinking. And, I've been lucky enough to receive the guidance of the Prinzessin der Verurteilung herself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! Who needs alcohol when you can make friends playing card games?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, need any tips from the master over here? You'll wipe the floor with that opponent of yours, Paimon guarantees it!

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, with the luck he's having, not even that legendary card-master from Sumeru could turn things around at this point.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... That last roll wasn't great. But who knows, maybe you'll have better luck next time?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: He keeps getting the exact same roll, over and over. This is the third time already.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seriously? That seems like a very unlikely coincidence...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: If there really is a god of fate, they could have cut this kid a bit of slack. Like, I don't know... make it possible for him to roll at least one other side of the dice?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I... think I've lost.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Must even a dragonborn, sanctified by the power of benediction, succumb to fate's insidious snares?

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Don't be sad, Durin! You'll definitely win the next round. You can even borrow Dodoco, if you want. Mom says she brings good luck!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Thanks, Klee, but there's something more important I need to take care of now.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Aww, okay...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the book's given us another hint, right?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Yep, and I think I've guessed where we're headed this time. C'mon, follow me.

talks.objective: Head to the Stormterror's Lair with Durin

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: In what sort of castle might a storybook dragon dwell?

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: The witch turned to a mighty dragon borne upon the wind to seek her answer.

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: From afar she beheld a solitary castle, standing lonely beneath its wings, and wrote it into words.

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: Its walls kept out the wind and rain, yet also cast a solemn shadow.

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: Enveloped by their shade, the story's boughs were lulled into a torpid slumber, and reached no further skyward.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: So that's the clue. I think we're meant to find a place where dragons live — and this time, in the real world.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I asked around, and it just so happens that there's a place like that in Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, that checks out...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I've heard that the dragon here is called Dvalin, and that he's a magnificent creature. I hope I get the chance to meet him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Wait a second!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think having the two of them meet is the best idea? Y'know, considering everything that happened in the past...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How would we even explain everything to him? Well, if we do run into Dvalin, it should turn out okay with us there at least.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Is something wrong?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope! Let's go!

choices.text: Yeah, it could be a problem...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: So this is where Dvalin lives?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, right into the middle of a raging storm...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: If you're afraid of getting blown away, Paimon, you can always hang onto my sleeve.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehehe, this isn't Paimon's first rodeo! C'mon, let's get going!

talks.objective: Enter the world within the book

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Not every day you're back in Mondstadt, huh? Care to grab a drink, if you're free?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, looks like we're back in the story world. And from the sounds of it, this chapter must be about Simulanka, right?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Yeah... Like the fairy from the Forest of Blessings, the King of Constellation Metropole, that cat lady who turns into a box...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, yep, that would be Nilou, Navia, and Kirara.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Oh, and there's Hat Guy too. Only...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Only...?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Only lately, whenever I see Hat Guy, I get this strange feeling...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What kind of feeling?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: It's like... there's something on his mind. He hasn't told me what it is, but I can sense it all the same.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, he's always been kinda... broody.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Hm... I guess I should focus on fulfilling my mother's final wish for now, though.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we should get started on this chapter. So, let's track you down and free you from fate's curse once again!

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: That day, a small band of adventurers suddenly arrived beneath the castle walls.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: They promised to help the little dragon cast off the curse of fate, yet as they stood beneath the castle walls, it appeared they had no idea how to even begin.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Instead of making fun of us, how about giving us a hint?

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: The little dragon had shut himself inside the tall tower at the castle's center. Anyone who wished to reach him must traverse the barriers that wall off his heart, for there is no other way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like we're in for another long one...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Let me try something...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oooh, do you have an idea?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: If that little dragon in the tower used to be me, then surely I'd know how he shuts people out better than anyone.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Come on, follow me.

choices.text: Next time you get the chance, just ask him.
It brings back a lot of memories.

talks.objective: Find a way to enter the castle
Defeat the opponents blocking your path

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, is that...?
Hah, a little pixie that can fly! Are you here to help the dragon break his curse too?
Oh, what's this? More brave adventurers bold enough to set foot in this castle? Come, join the ranks of your liege's guard!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nilou and Navia!?

dialogues.speaker: Flying Squirrel Fairy
dialogues.text: Nilou? No, no, no... I'm a flying squirrel fairy.

dialogues.speaker: Giraffe King
dialogues.text: And I'm a giraffe-king. Not this "Navia" you speak of.

choices.text: I don't think this is the real them.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: That's right... Oh, and don't forget cat-box lady.

response.speaker: Cat in a Box
response.text: Hm, are you friend or foe?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Friend! Definitely friend, Kira— Ahem, Miss, uh... cat-box lady.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, our companions from Simulanka are here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Simulanka is a big part of Durin's story. So, guess it's no surprise the people we were with there would make an appearance.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: ...Okay, I think I get it now. Flying squirrel fairy, giraffe king, cat-box lady — please, follow me.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: The shadows cast from the high walls of the tower were manifestations of the dragon's loneliness, barring the path of any visitor who wished to be his friend...

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: The group of brave creatures sought to aid the little dragon in lifting his curse, yet without light to lead the way, the group was trapped, waiting on a miracle...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Flying Squirrel Fairy
response.text: These shadows are blocking our path... It seems like the little dragon is afraid to meet us.

response.speaker: Giraffe King
response.text: Hmm, if only we had more firelight... But, you three don't seem to fear these shadows. Why?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Because... I carry more than enough "firelight" for all of us.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Besides, even though we're here to complete the story, who says it can't look a little different this time.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Before I met you all, I was so sure I'd never make a single friend. I pushed away anyone who tried to get close, until some kind of miracle brought you to me...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: This time, allow me to return the favor.

response.speaker: Flying Squirrel Fairy
response.text: I'm... not sure I followed all that, but you want to help the little dragon break his curse too, right?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Yes, so please, come with me!

choices.text: More like how Durin remembers them.

talks.objective: Continue going deeper into the castle

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Miss} Honorary Knight and Durin, are you heading off on a big adventure? But, but... Master Jean said I can't leave the city today. Promise me you'll tell me all about it when you get back, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: So be it... Such are fate's accursed wiles. Hmph!

talks.objective: Go to the young dragon's hideout

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come on, Durin! Or, um, little story dragon, just calm down!

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: Stay back! I don't wanna hurt you!

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Loneliness and fear had built a cage around his heart, shutting out all who would look upon him. And, thus, all the adventurers could see was his shadow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry. We can help you!

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: Don't come any closer!

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: And that was the last the little dragon spoke.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How are we supposed to persuade him if he won't even talk to us?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: This... really could have been how my story ended, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Back in Simulanka, I was no different.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: But even though I kept shutting everyone out, deep down I hoped someone would be strong enough to face my power and break through to me.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: And, that's exactly what you all did. I wouldn't be standing here today without you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: C'mon, let's bring this story full circle!

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Despite the little dragon's silence, once more the story-witch put pen to paper, and a miracle came to pass.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The flying squirrel fairy, the giraffe king, and cat-box lady arrived at the tower where the little dragon was hiding. But this time, guided by the miracle's light, they were able to traverse the shadows with ease.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Unafraid of the little dragon's claws and scales, they came to be his friends, just as he had hoped.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nilou, Navia, and Kirara?

choices.text: I don't think this is the real them.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: It's my friends from Simulanka...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: If you can still hear me, please listen to what I have to say.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Your claws and scales aren't some kind of inescapable curse, y'know. You'll overcome it one day, and make lots of new friends.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: I'm sure you think I'm lying. After all, no matter how many times you've tried to break it, nothing's ever worked.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: But this time is different — I brought your friends here to see you.

response.speaker: Little Dragon
response.text: ...Wh—What did you say?

response.speaker: Flying Squirrel Fairy
response.text: Hi, little dragon! I'm the flying squirrel fairy, and I'm here to help you lift your curse. Will you talk to me?

response.speaker: Giraffe King
response.text: And I'm the giraffe king! Don't be afraid, little one. We're not afraid of you.

response.speaker: Cat in a Box
response.text: I'm just a cat in a box... but I'd very much like to be your friend too.

response.speaker: Little Dragon
response.text: These are... my friends?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Yeah, they're your friends in the future you've been trying to avoid. I can promise you that.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: They're reaching out, so you just have to ask yourself one question... Do you accept?

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: After a long silence, heavy footsteps echoed from the tower's shadows — but still, the one who made them refused to step forward.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: Though the cage to his heart had been unlocked, the little dragon remained ashamed of his claws and scales.

response.speaker: Little Dragon
response.text: How can I face my friends like this?

response.speaker: Flying Squirrel Fairy
response.text: Don't worry, little dragon! We're gonna offer up our blessings and make a wish to the Goddess of Fate to release you from your curse.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, just like last time!

response.speaker: Little Dragon
response.text: Make a wish... to the Goddess of Fate?

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: At that moment, the merry-witch made her entrance.

response.speaker: Merry-Witch
response.text: Hello, little one — don't be afraid! With the blessings of your friends, your wish shall be granted.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alice? Wait, you're the "merry-witch" from the story?

response.speaker: Merry-Witch
response.text: Hahaha, correct! It is I, the merry-witch, creator-goddess of this realm. And it just so happens, the Goddess of Fate is none other than my dear friend, the story-witch.

response.speaker: Merry-Witch
response.text: I'm here to make good on my promise to lend her my second strongest spell.

response.speaker: Merry-Witch
response.text: With this spell, she'll have the power to create an entire world — so naturally, granting your wish won't be a problem. Provided, of course, you receive your friends' blessings...

response.speaker: Merry-Witch
response.text: But before we proceed, I must check something on her behalf. Little dragon, do you accept this blessing?

response.speaker: Little Dragon
response.text: I... I want to be your friend. So, if you're offering, then yes. I would love to have your blessings.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Of course, just like last time.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: Were it not for the adventurers' blessings, this tale might have ended long ago. Thanks to them, another ending was now possible.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: Yet in that moment, they did not know if this "blessing" was truly a gift or just another trial in disguise...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? You didn't say a word when we actually needed a clue, but now at a critical moment like this, you turn up and start playing mind-games...?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Another trial... Huh, that actually sounds about right. Be it the fictional problems of Simulanka or unavoidable conflicts in the real world, if you think about it, that's what they've been all along.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: But if it wasn't for those trials, I never would have met any of you. So despite all that, I'd still like to give my blessings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's the spirit! C'mon Durin, let's help you make your wish come true again!

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: On behalf of both my past and present selves — thank you, my friends.

choices.text: More like how Durin remembers them.

talks.objective: Discuss your experience within the story with Durin

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So Durin's wish came true, just like it did before!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: If this story was written by my mother, then surely that was the last chapter we just completed?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah... So, in other words, we finished it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehehe, looks like that's a wrap on Alice's task, and there's even some ink to spare!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Time to return the book, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess we'll have to wait for her to make contact, like she said.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: So, my mother's final story has finally come to a close...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like you're a little sad to see it end.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Back when I was still living in Simulanka, I was always under the illusion that my mother had never truly left.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Every day I spent immersed in that world, it felt like she was right there by my side, still reading me bedtime stories. But now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Durin...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we're all here for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! And you've got so many other friends waiting for you back in Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...Yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, after all that flying around, Paimon's starting to feel hungry again... so why don't we head back to Mondstadt? Perfect excuse for a big meal with the rest of the gang, hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now that you've fulfilled your mom's final wish, a little celebration seems in order, right?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: It's just a pity we never got to see that big, beautiful dragon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You were really looking forward to meeting him, huh... He might not be here all the time, but Paimon's sure you'll get a chance at some point!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Alright, no worries... Anyway, since this feast is to celebrate me fulfilling my mother's final wish, I guess it should be my little treat? Pretty sure that's how humans do it... right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Nuh-uh, this one's on {NICKNAME} and Paimon! Celebrating each other's achievements is what friends are for!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Honestly, when it comes to who treats who, human rules are so complicated...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: See? He wants to be friends with you too.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: But the moment hasn't come, at least not yet. In any case, the story should have a better ending this time, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew! Feels like we were gone for ages! Hopefully, everyone's still here...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: So your adventure was a success, huh? Wanna grab a drink to celebrate?

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Absolutely not! No booze allowed!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Miss} Honorary Knight! Durin! I wanna hear all about your big adventure!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're gonna order a big meal for everybody first — we'll talk while we eat!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Yippee!

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: Excuse me, did I hear you call him "Durin" just now? But, wasn't Durin the evil dragon that fell on Dragonspine?

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: C'mon Miss! This Durin isn't that evil dragon from Dragonspine! Albedo said... Um, well, it was kinda confusing... But anyway, it's super cool!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, is this your first time meeting him, Marjorie? Hehehe, no wonder you're getting him confused, haha...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Still... Even if you hadn't met him yet, shouldn't you have heard about him at the very least? At this point, pretty much the whole city has.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Uh... Why is everyone...

dialogues.speaker: Shuyun
dialogues.text: So, what exactly is his connection with the evil dragon?

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: Wait, but those horns on his head... Surely, he's not a...!?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Did everyone just... forget about Durin?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No. That... That can't be.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: ...The tricks of fate had just begun.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Watch out!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Stay calm!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: No one got hurt... did they?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Durin... Durin!

talks.objective: Check in with everyone about the current situation

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: I just had Barbara check him over. He's not badly hurt, but he seems to have burned through a lot of energy fending off some kind of dangerous power.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: He'll need some time to rest before he wakes up.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: So... can someone explain what's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: It seems like... aside from Durin's close acquaintances, the people of Mondstadt have forgotten everything about him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How could that even happen?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Worse still, the Abyssal power within him is showing signs of extreme instability. Could be a separate issue, though. I'm not sure.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: If the Abyssal power inside him spirals out of control, Mondstadt will be in grave danger...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe we should ask Albedo...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: I completely agree.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Alright then. As Acting Grand Master, I'll send a letter requesting Albedo's immediate return. Until then, the Knights will watch over Durin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's pretty much all we can do right now...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Also, allow me to look after this book for now. If you need to consult it, just drop by my <color=#37FFFF>office</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think... the book might have something to do with what's happening?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's possible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's just weird that Alice still hasn't contacted us... Maybe we should head back inside the book and take another look.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Fortunately, a brave band of adventurers heard tell of the little dragon's story.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Determined to lift his curse, they fought their way through countless trials.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: To help him, they offered up their blessings and made a wish to the Goddess of Fate.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: At last, their wish was granted. Shaking off his scales, the little dragon stepped out of the tower's gloom.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: But his time in the world beyond the castle would soon teach him... this gift would bring blessings and trials of its own.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: And, as far as the little dragon was concerned, the tricks of fate had just begun.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Ugh, where's that stench of booze coming fr— Agh, it's gotta be him... Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: No need to worry, he's stable for now.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: *sigh* Klee was really looking forward to hanging out with Durin. We'd better not tell her what's happened to him just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I'll have the Knights notify you as soon as he wakes up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look! Seems like someone's stuck down there.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Should they continue towards the tower, or plunge into the shadows to rescue those in need? A difficult dilemma indeed...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The path to the tower is up ahead. We'd better stick with Durin.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: You asked Barbara to tend to Durin and then settled him in a guest room.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Enveloped by their shade, the story's boughs were lulled into a torpid slumber, and reached no further skyward.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: And, as far as the little dragon was concerned, the tricks of fate had just begun.
